encounters.cc: Difficulty sleeping, persistent low mood, and tearfulness for 6 weeks following job loss

lines: Difficulty sleeping, persistent low mood, and tearfulness for 6 weeks following job loss

The patient is a 32-year-old female with established seasonal and perennial allergic rhinitis, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease who was evaluated in Otolaryngology three months prior for nasal congestion and allergic symptoms.

She presents to the Psychiatry clinic with difficulty sleeping, persistent low mood, and tearfulness for the past six weeks following an unexpected layoff from her marketing position, which she had held for the past five years.
She reports that she has been applying for new positions but has received few responses and feels discouraged.

She describes feeling irritable around friends and family and states that she "snaps at people more than usual." She denies suicidal ideation or feelings of hopelessness but admits that she "cries at random times." Her appetite has remained normal.
She continues to take care of her personal hygiene and responsibilities at home, but reports that she often lacks motivation and finds herself watching television most of the day.
She describes herself as normally "pretty upbeat" and states that she usually handles stress well, but notes that this job loss "really shook" her confidence.
She tried journaling and exercising but reports that her symptoms have not improved.

lines: Feeling overwhelmed, sad, and anxious for 3 weeks after unexpected job transfer

encounters.cc: Intermittent outbreaks of painful, slow-healing lesions on face and upper chest

lines: Intermittent outbreaks of painful, slow-healing lesions on face and upper chest

The patient is a 34-year-old female with a known history of aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease, chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, and prior outpatient treatment for adjustment disorder with anxiety, who presents to dermatology for evaluation of persistent skin lesions.
She reports that over the past several months she has developed intermittent outbreaks of painful, slow-healing lesions on her face and upper chest, sometimes accompanied by redness and swelling.
She was initially seen at two separate urgent care centers where she received topical antibiotics and corticosteroids with minimal improvement.

Concerned by the lack of response and the worsening appearance of her skin, she sought evaluation by a dermatologist who performed a biopsy and confirmed the diagnosis of an uncommon chronic inflammatory skin condition.
The dermatologist started her on topical therapy and referred her to primary care for continued management and counseling.

During the current visit, the patient appears frustrated and overwhelmed, explaining that she has spent hours reading about the disease online but is finding conflicting information that has made her more anxious.
She expresses concern about how this will affect her appearance long term, whether she'll have flares forever, and whether any of her internal organs might eventually be involved.
She asks the physician directly, "Have you seen this disease before? I just need someone who knows what I'm going through."

encounters.cc: Sudden-onset shortness of breath, facial flushing, and chest tightness after taking naproxen

lines: Sudden-onset shortness of breath, facial flushing, and chest tightness after taking naproxen

The patient is a 37-year-old female with aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (Samter's triad) and chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps, previously treated in Otolaryngology for allergic rhinitis and nasal septal perforation, who presents with acute respiratory symptoms.
She reports that she had been feeling well until this morning, when she woke up with generalized muscle soreness following an intense spin class the previous day.
For the soreness, she took one over-the-counter tablet of naproxen after breakfast.
Within 30–60 minutes, she began experiencing progressive fatigue, lightheadedness, and a sense of chest tightness, followed by wheezing and difficulty breathing.
She also felt flushed and noted puffiness around her eyes in the mirror.
She worried that her current symptoms might be panic-related but became alarmed when the wheezing and facial swelling developed.

She recalls a similar episode six months ago after taking an over-the-counter medication for a headache, though she did not seek medical care at that time.
She takes montelukast daily, which has helped with her nasal congestion and postnasal drip.
She also takes an oral contraceptive.
